current_answer: As of 21 October 2026, the public evidence reviewed still does not establish broad capability decline across popular AI models. BridgeBench’s latest listed tests (16 October) place all four displayed series within its 90–110 composite band; Claude Opus 5.5 is 105.8 relative to its first tracked session. That score mixes correctness, output tokens, and cost on a private 50-task suite. A new consumer thread reports memory and generic-response problems, but does not identify a verified model or surface or provide a matched replay. OpenAI’s 7 October release note says GPT-6 rolled into Chat while Work and Codex models were unchanged. This makes the exact surface and selected model a necessary check, not a proven cause. Before calling “GPT got worse” a model-wide change, record surface, model, effort, plan, context, and task, then replay a safe task under matched conditions.

catalogue_card.question: Did ChatGPT get worse—or did the product surface change?
catalogue_card.text: OpenAI documents a GPT-6 rollout in Chat on 7 October while Work and Codex models stayed separate. Fresh complaints lack matched tasks or a verified served-model receipt. Check the surface before treating them as one trend.

summary: No broad capability decline is established by this review of public evidence.

A new 21 October Reddit thread reports memory and generic-response problems, but supplies no matched task or verified model/surface. Replies describe both positive and negative experiences on different tasks.
OpenAI’s 7 October release notes distinguish the Chat rollout from Work and Codex; this is product context, not evidence that it caused any complaint.
BridgeBench’s latest listed tests are from 16 October; all four displayed series remain within the publisher’s 90–110 composite band. Opus 5.5 is 105.8 versus its first tracked session.
BridgeBench’s reference is its first tracked session; its composite includes correctness, output tokens, and cost, and public task-level component results are not shown.
For a completed weak answer, record the exact surface, model, plan, effort, context, and task before a safe matched replay; handle access errors separately.
uncertainty: The community thread is self-selected and cannot establish prevalence, a broad decline, or a causal link to the GPT-6 rollout.
The provider release note describes intended product changes; it does not verify which model served any individual user.
BridgeBench covers four series and a private task set, not every popular model, route, user task, or account.
BridgeBench’s first-session reference, composite, and stated band are publisher methodology; the public board does not show task-level results, component scores, or model-specific variance intervals.
The last dated LiveNerf update reviewed in the previous cycle was 17 October; its second window was incomplete then.
Analytics were unavailable, so pool discovery, reader action, repeat use, switching, and commercial outcomes were not measured.
freshness_note: Reviewed 21 October 2026. New user reports make the Chat versus Work/Codex product boundary salient, but no matched task evidence establishes a broad capability decline.
